newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Korean officials discuss peace negotiations.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Korean officials discuss peace negotiations.

text.p: U.S., North and South Korean officials met in New York Thursday for the second time in a week to try to narrow differences over proposed four-party Korean peace talks, the State Department said.
The department's Korea office director Mark Minton led the U.S. delegation. Names of the North and South Korean negotiators were not immediately available.

The talks aim to win Pyongyang's acceptance of a U.S.-South Korean proposal launched last year to hold negotiations, also involving China, on a peace treaty to replace the armistice that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
North Korea agreed in principle to such negotiations in April, but has made its final acceptance conditional on receiving major food aid from the United States.
Washington says it can give such aid only when the talks are under way. It has sent limited grain shipments to North Korea to help avert a serious famine there.
